title: Running a dense air temperature measurement field campaign at the urban neighbourhood level: Protocol and lessons learned
author: Kraemer, Remmler, et al.

steps.title: Define study design
steps.instruction: Specify the study objectives, select the two inner‑city parks in Leipzig, Germany, and decide the measurement period (hot, dry summer), answering the What, When, Where, and How questions.

steps.title: Start preparations early
steps.instruction: Begin preparation in spring 2018, roughly four months before the first campaign, to allow sufficient time for all subsequent actions.

steps.title: Conduct site visits
steps.instruction: Visit each park to locate suitable measuring spots, identify fenced areas, decide exact sensor positions, assess soil conditions, and note required tools for soil management.

steps.title: Select and acquire sensors
steps.instruction: Choose appropriate dense‑air‑temperature sensors for the campaign and purchase them.

steps.title: Develop and acquire equipment
steps.instruction: Design or obtain all necessary mounting hardware, power supplies, data loggers, and any other field equipment required for sensor deployment.

steps.title: Obtain official authorizations
steps.instruction: Identify the correct city administration contacts and land‑owner representatives, request permission for sensor installation (including fenced sites), and allow several weeks for response; verify the rightful owners of each fenced location.

steps.title: Plan personnel and logistics
steps.instruction: Create a staffing schedule covering a four‑week period for a planned seven‑day measurement campaign, include flexibility for weather‑dependent adjustments (2–3 days forecast), arrange logistics for equipment transport, and inform all team members that work may be required on weekends.
